questions.question: Why use `collections.deque` instead of a list for a BFS queue?
options: deque uses less memory per element than any other container
deque supports O(1) pops from the left, while list.pop(0) is O(n)
lists cannot hold more than 2**16 items
questions.explanation: deque offers O(1) appends and pops at both ends. list.pop(0) shifts every remaining element, making it O(n).

questions.question: What must you do before using `itertools.groupby` to group all equal keys together?
options: Sort the data by the same key function
Convert the data to a set
Wrap the data in a deque
Nothing; groupby collects all equal keys automatically
questions.explanation: groupby only groups consecutive items with equal keys, so unsorted input produces repeated, fragmented groups.

questions.question: What happens if you call an `@lru_cache`-decorated function with a list argument?
options: The list is converted to a tuple automatically
The call succeeds but is not cached
A TypeError is raised because list is unhashable
questions.explanation: lru_cache uses arguments as dictionary keys, so every argument must be hashable. Lists are not.

questions.question: What happens when you subtract a timezone-aware datetime from a naive one?
options: The naive value is assumed to be UTC
The result is a timedelta in local time
The naive value is assumed to be local time
questions.explanation: Python refuses to mix naive and aware datetimes in arithmetic or comparisons, raising TypeError. Store and compute in aware UTC.
